To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IBDV-encoded protease VP4 can form intracellular amyloid fibrils via the C-terminal hydrophobically and amyloidogenic peptide, and this assembly of VP4 can facilitate viral replication.
the Avibirnaviruses VP4 can self-assemble into tubules in the infected cell and the assembly is mediated by the last C-terminal amyloid-forming region of VP4.
VP4 can form intracellular tubules and fibrils during IBDV infection and these fibrils are essential for IBDV lytically infecting cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the formation mechanism and functions of VP4 fibrils, which may help understand the molecular basis of Avibirnaviruses infection and provide potential therapeutic strategies against Avibirnavirues diseases.
the self-assembly of the Avibirnavirus protease VP4 and the potential role of fibrils in IBDV infection.
the formation and potential biological functions mechanism of Avibirnaviruses viral protease-related fibrillar structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Avibirnaviruses protease VP4 can assemble in a C-terminal amyloid-like manner to form fibrils and filaments in IBDV infected cells, which is essential for the viral replication and lytic infection.
VP4 can initiate the self-assembly into fibrils at early stage of viral replication.
VP4 forms fibrils in a cell-type independent manner and the fibril formation is a key step to regulate the VP4 cytotoxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Avibirnaviral VP4 self-assembly is an essential and conserved process during viral infection.

the Avibirnaviridae viral protease VP2/VP4 initiates the formation of fibrillar structures in the early stage of viral infection, the formation of fibrils is not dependent on other viral protein or host cytoskeletal proteins, the C-terminal hydrophobics and amyloidogenic residues play a critical role in the formation of VP4 fibrils, which potentially facilitate the viral replication and lytic infection.

VP4 can form intracellular fibrillar structures in diverse IBD cells, and this process doesn’t depend on the host cytoskeletal system, other viral proteins and vital subcellular compartments, and the last C-terminal amyloid-forming sequence is the key determinant for VP4 assembly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminal amyloid-forming region of the Avibiravirus viral protease contributes to self- assembly of Avibirnaviral protease and plays important roles in the viral infection.
VP4 forms intracellular tubules during viral infection.
VP4 can self-assemble into fibrils in the cytoplasm of IBDV infected cells, which is a novel feature among viral proteases.
